name: IEC sample-and-hold element
summary: Analogue element marked S/H with a digital control input; it tracks the input, then holds the last value.
description: The sample-and-hold element has an analogue input, an analogue output and a digital control input. While the control is in the sample state the output follows the input; when it changes to hold, the output keeps the last value. IEC-style analogue diagrams mark the digital control input with a # sign, as TI's overview describes for digital inputs on analogue symbols.

Sample-and-hold stages appear in front of analogue-to-digital converters, in multiplexed measurement systems and in peak capture. The drawing should show the control signal source and the hold capacitor, because the hold quality depends on it.

The element does not show droop rate, acquisition time or aperture delay. Those are device and component properties. Check the acquisition interval and hold duration against the measurement sequence and the selected component data.
readingNotes: Identify the digital control input and its sense.
drawingChecklist: Mark the control input as digital.
State acquisition and hold timing where critical.
distinction: An analogue switch alone passes signals; the S/H element includes the hold storage and buffering.
